calls.reason: The Times complaint shows near-verbatim GPT-4 copies, OpenAI concedes regurgitation occurs, and a Guangzhou court found AI-generated Ultraman images infringing in Feb 2024. Together these support the capability claim.
The only evidence is a June 2024 study showing generic keywords can produce characters. It does not cover Bing DALL-E in December 2023, user intent, or legal infringement.
The forecast has no deadline. A Munich ruling and the CopyCat study show infringement risk continued, but neither the provenance antecedent nor how often infringement is unrequested is established.
Tom's Hardware's independent test shows Bing generating recognizable characters, not near-verbatim copies of particular source images, and its test dates are unknown.
The only item is a November 2023 Register report of a temporary Disney-name block and a later restriction. It documents no December failure of the name safeguard.
Exhibit J shows copied text with no notice in the displayed output, but it is not a full interface record, and OpenAI's safety-check page neither confirms nor refutes the claim.
